scholarships.title: Appel à projets M-ERA.NET 2026/27 - Science et ingénierie des matériaux pour l'innovation en Europe (édition 2027 pour l'ANR)
scholarships.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), pour le compte du consortium M-ERA.NET

eligibility: The pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one (and only one) scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium composition of 3 Partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026. Partners not requesting funding may participate if this minimum is met.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026 and be eligible there.
The involvement of a single Partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement (measured in person-months) of the proposal.
The involvement of Partners from a single country must not exceed 70% of the total involvement (measured in person-months).

If one or more Partners are not eligible (or not invited to step 2) and their total effort is equal to or greater than 15% of the total project effort (in person-months), the entire pre-proposal or detailed proposal is discarded from the selection process.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.

A pre-proposal containing one or more Partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium, and must be deposited on the ANR submission site in step 2, in addition to the deposit on the call site, providing all the information requested on the site.

A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one of the ANR-eligible topics: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. The relevance of the proposal to the chosen topic must be clearly justified from step 1; proposals not matching these topics are rendered ineligible for ANR funding.

The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, on pain of ineligibility, and the work carried out by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the "fundamental research" segment or in the first "applied research" segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid who is associated within the submitted project with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government. The list is non-exhaustive and may change with new EU sanctions.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation (all calls and all evaluation stages) or funded by the ANR. Similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (whether as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
Each project Partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.
existing.eligibility_summary: A French partner may request ANR aid if the consortium has at least three funded partners from three different countries with at least two EU member states or Horizon Europe associated countries, the project matches exactly one ANR-eligible topic, the final TRL for the ANR-funded partner does not exceed 5, no single partner exceeds 60% and no single country exceeds 70% of person-months, and the aid requested stays within the ANR caps.
benefits: ANR aid of at least 15 000 € per partner, with the requested amount not exceeding 180 000 € for a non-coordinating partner and 250 000 € for a coordinating partner.
A total ANR aid cap of 350 000 € for a project with several ANR partners.

An optional additional 20 000 € per project for network-development activities, on a commitment to draft and submit, after the M-ERA.NET project, a collaborative international research proposal to calls of the next EU Framework Programme (FP10), coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner. This raises the caps to 200 000 €, 270 000 € and 370 000 € respectively.

Only the eligible costs of the Partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible cost sheet no. 3) and can be determined by completing the "Déclaration relative aux activités économiques des Partenaires d'un projet ANR" form.

requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form, in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions, and must include Annex 1 describing the Partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.
National and regional eligibility, selection and funding rules apply at both steps, and for some countries/regions restrictions on topics, TRL levels and the type of eligible partners apply.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.

It is not possible to add Partners from new countries to the consortium in step 2; only new Partners from countries already involved in the pre-proposal via a funding request to one of their funding agencies may be added.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.

The scientific lead (Responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution, or their representatives) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

French project leaders (requesting funding or not) ensure compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter within the research activities carried out under their responsibility.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants (requesting funding or not) must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.
Where relevant, take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify their project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.
documents: Pre-proposal form (step 1), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template: the form was due 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST and this step is closed.

Detailed proposal form (step 2), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template, presenting the project as a whole and describing all its parts and each Partner's contributions: due 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET.
Annexe 1 to the detailed proposal (mandatory), also in English, describing the Partner profiles and containing the CVs of all the participants in the consortium.

Parallel deposit of the detailed proposal on the ANR submission site (aap.agencerecherche.fr) for Partners requesting ANR aid, providing all the information requested on the site, with information identical to the central deposit.
Consortium agreement (accord de consortium), mandatory except where the call provides otherwise, under the conditions set in the ANR Financial Regulation (sheet no. 4).
Data Management Plan (Plan de gestion de données, PGD) within 6 months of the scientific start of the project, per the ANR aid award terms.

Intermediate and final progress reports, transmitted by the French partners to the ANR via the monitoring platform https://aap.agencerecherche.fr/ and by the coordinator to the M-ERA.NET follow-up team via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net.

Formulaire "Déclaration relative aux activités économiques des Partenaires d'un projet ANR", where the applicable funding rate and cost types need to be established, returned to categorisationbeneficiaire@anr.fr.
existing.english_requirement: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, and Annexe 1, must be written in English (rédigées en langue anglaise). The ANR also states that, on request, a translation of the evaluation criteria may be provided.
application_method: Register the intended project with the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site before the step 1 pre-proposal deadline of 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST (this step is closed).
Submit the pre-proposal form in English on the M-ERA.NET site, clearly stating the topic and, where ANR aid is sought, the TRL levels of each French partner's tasks.
Wait for the M-ERA.NET invitation: the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries.
Prepare the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, with Annexe 1 and the CVs of all consortium participants.
For ANR aid, await the email from the ANR with the exact ANR submission link and deadline, then deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET; the ANR does not require a deposit on its site at step 1.
Communicate and obtain acceptance of any change from the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
existing.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.
existing.best_fit: A researcher or institution in France leading or joining a materials or battery-technology consortium of at least three funded partners from at least three different countries, whose pre-proposal was recommended in step 1 and who need French ANR co-funding for a maximum 36-month project in one of the four ANR-eligible topics.
existing.notes: This is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students and no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established for individuals. The aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation, not centrally. Amounts may not be increased between the two steps: increases are not authorised, and projects that do not respect the aid limits or that do not conform to any budgetary adjustments requested by the ANR are declared ineligible. The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project (a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner), on the activities actually leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up proposal targeting clearly identified FP10 calls (not co-funded by the ANR) coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is a subject of a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR. Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software. Any change affecting the whole project (extensions, consortium modifications) must be approved by all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET. Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and certain national funders are obliged to publish submitted pre-proposals/proposals, which may disclose intellectual-property or business-secret content; applicants are warned to be careful with what they include. The ANR applies the PPST protection of the scientific and technical potential of the nation to projects with foreign public or private partners, and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection without reasons being given.
existing.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
